newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Valecom, CSN win new partners in Brazil CVRD bid.
newsitem.headline: Valecom, CSN win new partners in Brazil CVRD bid.

text.p: Brazilian metal and metallurgical group Caemi will join the Valecom consortium to bid for state mining giant CVRD, while four pension funds have joined the CSN group.
On April 29, the government is selling a 40-45 percent voting stake in CVRD for three billion reais ($2.83 billion).
"Everything indicates that Caemi will be joining Valecom," said a spokesman for Caemi. "Talks are more or less being held with this understanding."
The CSN-led consortium, which includes Nations Bank, South Africa's Gencor and Opportunity Asset Management, has signed a deal with four pension funds, Previ, Petros, Funcef and Funcesp.
The four pension funds already have a joint voting stake of around 10 percent in CVRD, which would give the CSN consortium a controling position in CVRD if it wins the auction.
CSN is also holding talks with Brazilian pulp and paper group Suzano, construction firm Camargo Correia and U.S. aluminium company Alcoa.

The Valecom consortium is being led by Brazilian metal, cement and pulp group Votorantim and South Africa's Anglo-American Corp and also includes pension funds Centrus and Sistel, which have an existing joint stake in CVRD of 2.8 percent.
Valecom is also expected to have a strong Japanese presence with a group of 12 Japanese steelmakers and trading companies led by Nippon Steel.
Caemi also has a strong Japanese connection. Mitsui & Co recently invested $180 million in Caemi's increase in share capital and now holds a 40 percent stake in the company.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151)) (c) Reuters Limited 1997
